methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Series A → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.0x) to $50M total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 3 same-sector + same/adjacent-stage peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.1B - $1.8B.

data.narrative:
AIM Intelligent Machines is a Series A robotics and manufacturing company that has raised $50M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a comp universe of 9 private robotics firms and 1 public company (277810.KQ), with particular weight given to three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage peers: Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B Series B), Dexterity ($1.6B Series B), and Walden Robotics ($1.1B Seed).

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total capital raised as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical of Series A progression, implies a $100M valuation. Peer-median analysis across the three-company comp set yields a $1.6B implied valuation, with the peer range spanning $1.1B to $1.8B. The wide dispersion reflects stage heterogeneity within the peer set—two Series B companies and one Seed stage—and inherent valuation volatility in early-stage robotics.

Triangulating these two methods produces a valuation range of $85M (low) to $1.9B (high), with a median of $875M. The wide band reflects genuine uncertainty: stage-progression analysis systematically underweights the company relative to later-stage comparables, while peer-median analysis may not fully discount for AIM's earlier stage relative to Series B peers. Key uncertainties include revenue traction and capital efficiency relative to the peer set, which are not detailed in available data.
